context:
Start from the current public contract taxonomy, then add benchmark-specific
evidence dimensions. Use the registry to enumerate benchmark IDs and statuses.
Cross-check docs and result-integrity spec coverage, then write a compact
matrix that explains current status values without becoming a second runtime
catalog. Add a drift check only after choosing a matrix format that can be
parsed reliably.
description:
PR #502 added registry-owned `support_status` for every benchmark, but the
first assignment is still a product decision encoded as metadata rather than
an auditable criteria matrix. The current counts are test-protected, but the
repository does not yet explain why each benchmark is stable, beta,
experimental, repo_only, deprecated, or document_only.

Build a benchmark support-status criteria matrix that makes future promotions
and demotions reviewable. The matrix should evaluate each benchmark against
concrete product criteria: user docs coverage, result-integrity spec coverage,
dataset/source contract, validation coverage, public discovery behavior,
DataFrame coverage where claimed, known unsupported platform gaps, and
maintenance commitment. The matrix should not duplicate the registry as a
second source of truth; it should document the rationale and acceptance
thresholds for changing the registry-owned status field.

anti_patterns.dont: change DataFrame capability flags as part of criteria documentation
anti_patterns.instead: file follow-up TODOs for capability gaps.
anti_patterns.why: capability and support status are separate contracts

anti_patterns.dont: duplicate the entire BENCHMARK_METADATA table in docs
anti_patterns.instead: document only status rationale and evidence pointers.

anti_patterns.dont: mark a benchmark stable only because it imports or runs at smoke scale
anti_patterns.why: stable implies docs, validation, and maintenance commitment

anti_patterns.dont: use benchmark category as status rationale
anti_patterns.why: category is workload taxonomy, not product support

deferrals.reason: It is the only beta whose sole integrity-dimension gap is a missing result-integrity spec; adding one (plus a DataFrame routing decision) is the concrete blocker recorded in docs/benchmarks/support-status.md.
deferrals.summary: Promote vector_search beta -> stable once it has a BenchmarkSpec

deferrals.reason: Their status is partly coupled to the benchbox.core.base_benchmark.BaseBenchmark migration; revisit when that base is gone.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] conditional-unmet: Verified benchbox/core/base_benchmark.py still exists; deprecated base has not been removed, so the reassessment trigger has not occurred.
deferrals.summary: Reassess tpcds_obt and datavault experimental status after the deprecated core base is removed

deferrals.reason: External-dataset betas are gated on a pinned source contract, not on query coverage.
deferrals.summary: Pin reproducible external-source contracts for nyctaxi and flightdata before any stable promotion

preserves.behavior: Benchmark surface visibility remains independent of support_status.
Current public benchmark discovery count remains unchanged unless a separate surface decision changes it.
Runtime support_status values remain registry-owned in benchbox/core/benchmark_registry.py.
supports_dataframe remains a capability flag, not a proxy for support status.

prior_art.concept: benchbox/core/benchmark_registry.py: BENCHMARK_METADATA support_status values - reuse as runtime source of truth.
docs/development/result-integrity-validation.md: integrity spec coverage list - use as one evidence dimension, not as the whole support decision.
docs/platforms/support-status.md: platform support-status rationale style - reuse the explanatory pattern, but adapt criteria to benchmark-specific evidence.
docs/reference/public-contracts.md: support taxonomy and count policy - extend criteria language rather than creating new status terms.
tests/unit/core/test_benchmark_api_contract.py: benchmark count and support-status drift tests - extend for matrix row coverage.

verifications.description: Benchmark registry support-status contract remains green.
verifications.expected: All benchmark API contract tests pass.

work_units.notes:
Capture the checked SHA, current status counts, benchmark IDs, public IDs,
and result-integrity spec coverage in the TODO or implementation PR body.
Do not rely on the PR #502 review text alone; the criteria matrix must be
based on the current tree at implementation time.
work_units.summary: Re-read the benchmark registry, public contract map, benchmark docs, and result-integrity spec list before proposing criteria

work_units.notes:
Write criteria for stable, beta, experimental, repo_only, deprecated, and
document_only. Include benchmark-specific dimensions that platform status
did not need: official-vs-development scale factors, generated-vs-external
datasets, canonical query coverage, result validation availability, docs
depth, and whether DataFrame support is claimed for that benchmark.
work_units.summary: Define status-specific acceptance criteria for benchmark families

work_units.notes:
Produce one row per benchmark with the current registry status, rationale,
evidence pointers, and any promotion/demotion blockers. The matrix may live
in a developer/reference doc, but the runtime status remains in
`benchbox/core/benchmark_registry.py`.
work_units.summary: Score every registry benchmark against the criteria and record status rationale

work_units.notes:
Add a focused test that fails when a benchmark status is added, removed, or
changed without a corresponding criteria-matrix row or explicit rationale
update. Prefer a simple parseable markdown table or YAML/JSON summary if
the existing docs test patterns can check it cleanly.
work_units.summary: Add tests or docs checks that keep the matrix synchronized with registry status values

work_units.notes:
If the matrix shows that a beta benchmark is close to stable or that an
experimental benchmark has unclear criteria, record follow-up TODOs or
deferred entries with exact blockers. Do not change support_status values
in this TODO unless the criteria evidence makes the change unambiguous.
work_units.summary: Record concrete promotion candidates and blockers as deferred work, not as silent comments
